supported_context_single_chip.basis: Phase 1 of the design: single-chip functional layers with the sparse DSA path validated up to 16385 tokens (tests/test_dsa_long.py::test_sparse_16k, layer 3 vs HF: prefill PCC 0.99983, rows < 2048 0.99988, rows >= 2048 0.99980, decode at 16385/16386 0.99996/0.99995). The advertised 1 048 576 positions are the Phase 2 multi-chip (8x4) contract with the user-partitioned paged latent cache.
supported_context_single_chip.hard_limit_note: (i) Decode: not capacity-bound on one chip for a single user at the advertised 1 M positions: 11 DSA layers x 1,048,576 positions x 512 x 2 B = 11 GiB of latent pages + pooled keys (one [128] bf16 row per 4 tokens = 64 B/token: 11 x 262,144 x 256 B = 0.69 GiB) + 2 x 32 x 128 x 2 B ring rows per user and layer, against 31.83 GiB allocatable DRAM (measured: 8 banks x 3.979 GiB, 7.35 GiB resident after the layer-3 build, _logs/fix3_perf_layer3_prefill.log); the single-chip decode bound is validation time of the v1 composite paths. (ii) Single-shot prefill: capacity-bound. For a prompt of T tokens (S = T - 2048 sparse query rows, W = 32 * ceil(max_seq_len / 128) pooled-key columns, about T/4) the peak sits inside TtDSAIndexer.select at the 4x repeat_interleave of the scores (ttnn repeat_interleave along the last dim = transpose, 4x concat, transpose back): the TILE scores [S, W] bf16, their ROW_MAJOR copy, the transposed copy, the repeated [4W, S] and the result [S, 4W] are live together = 22 * S * W bytes (about 5.5 * T^2), plus the tensors held across the call: fp32 streams [T, 16384] (64 KiB/row), pre-norm + normalized input (16 KiB/row), q [T, 16384] bf16 (32 KiB/row), q_resid (3 KiB/row), the sparse-row slices x_s / qr_s and the indexer queries [32, S, 128] (19 KiB/row), the dense-row output [2048, 16384] bf16 (64 MiB) and the caches (1 KiB latent + 64 B pooled keys per token); the next-highest point, sparse_sdpa (q_rm + o_rm [64, S, 512] bf16 = 128 KiB/row, kv_rm, indices [S, 2176] u32), is linear in T. Evaluated: T = 16385 -> 1.21 GiB quadratic, 3.35 GiB peak (the validated point); 32768 -> 9.4 GiB; 49152 -> 18.3 GiB; largest single-shot T within the 24.48 GiB free next to the 7.35 GiB layer-3 weights = 58368 (peak 24.4 GiB; computed, not validated). The 16385 validated point stands; chunked prefill (in progress on another branch) scores [T_chunk, W] per chunk and removes this bound.

largest_tested.decode_evidence: sparse decode at 16385/16386 (0.99996/0.99995), 4097..4108 on a random prompt (>= 0.9997, selection 98-99 % of HF ids, index rows contiguous and in range, pool cache 0.99999 vs host), dense->sparse 2040..2063 (>= 0.99962, short user 0 >= 0.9995 every step), 2042/2043 prompts decoded through the pool completion and across 2050/2051 (>= 0.99978), dense 256..259 / 1000..1002, traced replay == eager, 8 users (worst per-user 0.99938 layer 3, 0.999363 layer 4)

cache_and_position_semantics.kda_state: per user: recurrent [1,64,128,128] fp32 + conv history [1,3,24576] bf16, written by prefill into fixed user slots of a persistent [max_batch,...] state; decode updates all slots in place (trace-safe)
cache_and_position_semantics.dsa_latent_cache: paged [max_blocks,1,32,512] bf16 per layer; page table [max_batch, blocks_per_seq] with any unique block mapping (tested: identity and random permutations); prefill fills a user's pages from position 0, decode appends at the user's position
cache_and_position_semantics.dsa_index_cache: pooled keys [max_batch*pool_blocks,1,32,128] bf16 (one row per 4 tokens, identity table) + per-user 32-row raw k/gate rings (row = position % 4); maintained on every prefill and decode call, dense or sparse
cache_and_position_semantics.positions: DecodePositions: persistent [B] int32 device tensors (position, position // 4, position % 4) plus the host values; refreshed in place per step (trace-replay safe); the host values select the sparse path
cache_and_position_semantics.mode_switch: DSA layers: a query sees every visible token while floor((a+1)/4) <= 512, i.e. positions <= 2050, so the dense attention is HF-exact there. Prefill: rows [0, 2048) dense, rows >= 2048 indexer + sparse_sdpa (those rows always see >= 2048 pooled tokens, so the index row is a full valid prefix as sparse_sdpa requires). Decode: dense flash-MLA for every user slot, users at position >= 2051 get the per-user sparse result (mixed batches stay exact for short users). Tested across the boundary at 2040..2063 (prompt tails 0, 1, 2, 3).
cache_and_position_semantics.batch: fixed user slots: decode batch == max_batch; tested max_batch 1, 2, 8 and 32 (prompt lengths 1..200 mixed, permuted page table, tests/test_batch8.py). B=32 runs on both layer kinds: the flash-MLA decode gets 120 cores (12x10 grid, min(grid, 4*32)) = 3 cores per user (96 active, 2 tree-reduction rounds); layer 4 passed (prefill worst 0.999937, decode worst per user 0.999698 / 0.999944 over 2 steps, _logs/fix3_batch8_B32-4.log); layer 3: all 64 decode samples > 0.995 (worst per user 0.997380 / 0.999489, _logs/fix3_batch8_B32-3.log) but the case fails the per-user prefill gate (0.995, not lowered) on user 18 (S=5, offset 1620 of the R4097 stream): pcc 0.994797 with one of its five rows at 0.98025 (median 0.99992): a short prompt is a handful of draws of the per-row PCC distribution (over the 32 prompts' 2542 rows: 21 rows < 0.997, min 0.98025); the 0.98025 row is HF's 8th routed expert swapped for its 9th on a near-tied score (_logs/fix3_router_flip_user18.log), see capability_reductions (per-row tail). B=8 (3 steps): decode worst per user 0.999377 layer 3 / 0.999363 layer 4 (_logs/fix3_batch8_B8.log).
cache_and_position_semantics.traced_decode: capturable for every layer kind; refused for DSA decoders whose max_seq_len > 2051 unless allow_sparse_range (dense attention past 2050 is not HF semantics); the sparse decode rows run eagerly from host positions
cache_and_position_semantics.prefill: single-shot: one chunk from position 0 per user (chunked prefill with actual_start is not wired through the public API)

capability_reductions.status: deferred to Phase 2 (8x4 mesh, user-partitioned cache)

capability_reductions.item: indexer scores ranked at bf16 resolution
capability_reductions.status: quantified: 98-99 % of the HF-selected ids per step, layer PCC >= 0.9997
capability_reductions.risk: boundary pools differ from the fp32 HF ranking; an fp32 scoring path is a Phase 2/3 option if token-level accuracy shows a gap

capability_reductions.status: not delivered in stage 1 (single-shot prefill only; ttKDA carries and the DSA cache support it, the FunctionalDecoder API does not expose it)
capability_reductions.risk: the sparse prefill's score expansion (22 * S * W bytes live at the 4x repeat_interleave, about 5.5 * T^2: 1.2 GiB at 16385, 18 GiB at 49152) is the practical single-chip single-shot prefill bound: about 58368 tokens next to the layer-3 weights (computed, not validated; see supported_context_single_chip.hard_limit_note); chunked prefill removes it

capability_reductions.item: per-row PCC tail on MoE layers (near-tie routed-expert swaps)
capability_reductions.status: quantified on layer 3: 21/2542 rows < 0.997 (min 0.98025) over the 32 B=32 prompts; every low row checked on device is HF's 8th routed expert swapped for its 9th at a biased-score gap <= 3e-3 (user 18 row 4: pcc 0.980249, gap 2.95e-3, HF-only [188] TT-only [266]; row 1: 0.998170, gap 2.78e-4; the 1-token B=8 user: 0.996787, gap 1.35e-3; rows with identical sets 0.9999; _logs/fix3_router_flip_user18.log); the 8th/9th gap is < 1e-3 for 18 % and < 3e-3 for 39 % of the tokens of a 512-token prompt, so swaps are common but usually cheap (the 8th weight is the smallest)
capability_reductions.risk: a 1..5-row prompt is a handful of draws of this distribution and can fall below a 0.995 per-user PCC gate (tests/test_batch8.py B=32 layer 3, user 18 S=5: 0.994797; bar kept, that case is red on this draw while all 64 decode samples pass); the token-level effect is measured on the full model, an fp32 router input is the Phase 2/3 option
